passage: All of July, Urmila sat on the steps of the village library after school and read her History notes cover to cover, twice a day. She could almost see the pages with her eyes shut. Then the August unit test came back: 34, up from 31. A whole month for three marks. On the bus home, Devika showed her own paper, 52, and a stack of small slips. "I close the book and answer questions from the old papers. Then I check." Urmila was quiet the whole ride. That night she shut her notebook and tried five questions from last year's paper, no peeking. She could fully answer only two. Causes of the 1857 revolt? Blank. So much for reading it thirty times. At least now she knew where the holes were.

qa.q: What did Urmila score in the August unit test?
What might Urmila have felt during the quiet bus ride?
qa.a: She probably felt disappointed and frustrated at a month of reading giving only three marks, and uneasy seeing Devika's 52.

qa.q: What would you suggest Urmila do with the blank questions?
qa.a: Study those topics, like the causes of the 1857 revolt, then test herself again with the book shut, so practice keeps pointing to what she doesn't know.

qa.q: How might Devika feel sharing the method?
qa.a: Devika may be glad to help but a little awkward showing a higher score, hoping Urmila takes it as help, not showing off.

grounding: Shows a student noticing a month of rereading barely moved her score and switching to closed-book questions that reveal her gaps.

passage: For four weeks Ines reread her Biology notes every evening in her room in Lisbon, highlighter in hand, until the pages glowed yellow. Her quiz scores barely moved: 11, 12, 11 out of 20. On Thursday she threw the highlighter across the desk. "I know this stuff. Why doesn't it show?" Soo-ah, who lived downstairs and was studying for the same exam, came up with a stack of index cards. "Close the notes. Answer these." Ines got the first one, then stalled on how enzymes work, then on osmosis. "I recognise it when I read it," she said slowly. "I can't produce it." That night she wrote her own question cards, fifteen of them, and answered them with the notebook shut. Three topics came up blank every time.

qa.q: What were Ines's quiz scores during the four weeks?
What does Ines throwing the highlighter show?
qa.a: It shows she felt frustrated and stuck, working hard every evening while the scores barely moved.

qa.q: What should Ines do with the three blank topics?
qa.a: Relearn those topics first and keep testing them on cards with the notes shut, instead of rereading everything equally.

qa.q: What is it like for Soo-ah to watch Ines struggle?
qa.a: Soo-ah seems to care enough to come up with cards, and may feel useful seeing the questions finally show where the gaps are.

grounding: Shows a student realising weeks of rereading aren't working and switching to closed-book question cards that reveal weak spots.
